summary: Researchers found that attackers ran an autonomous AI agent in unattended mode to explore and map the network of Thailand's Ministry of Finance. They found signs of compromise but no data theft, and the ministry has not confirmed a breach.
technical_summary: An open-source AI agent was run in an unattended mode that skips approval prompts, automating post-compromise reconnaissance, file searching and privilege-escalation checks alongside conventional exploits and a custom backdoor. Exposed attacker directories revealed the agent logs.

severity.quote: the researchers said they found no indication that data had been exfiltrated

notes: The ministry has not confirmed a breach, and some artifacts show only that systems were targeted.

summary: A popular free VPN browser extension was updated to capture users' conversations with AI chatbots and share the data with an affiliated data broker, with no way to turn it off. Millions of users were reportedly affected.
technical_summary: An update added scripts injected into AI chat sites that intercept prompts and responses plus metadata, enabled by default regardless of VPN state. The data was shared with an affiliated analytics company, and the store listing contradicted the privacy practices.

harm_type.quote: A popular Google Chrome browser extension has been found to be harvesting anything its users prompted into most of the biggest AI tools around

affected_population.quote: Urban VPN Proxy has more than six million installations

notes: The AI chatbots were the data source, not the cause; the harm stems from the extension's data collection.

summary: A former lawyer for a former US president said he used Google Bard to find case citations, which his attorney then included in a court filing. The judge could not find the cases because they did not exist.
technical_summary: Google Bard generated realistic-looking but fictitious legal citations. The user did not understand that the tool can fabricate sources and passed them on, and they were submitted to a federal court without verification.

summary: The FTC and DOJ charged Amazon with keeping children's Alexa voice recordings indefinitely and ignoring parents' deletion requests, partly to improve its voice recognition. Amazon agreed to pay a fine and delete certain data.
technical_summary: Alexa's default data handling retained children's voice recordings and transcripts, kept them after deletion requests, and reused them to refine voice recognition algorithms, which the FTC said violated COPPA and misled parents about deletion.
